'''John Simpson''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FInstP}} (born 23 March 1958) is a British nuclear physicist. He is known for his work in gamma-ray spectroscopy and detector design. He was Head of Technology, Division of Technology Department.<ref>{{citation |title=Division of Technology Department STFC Daresbury Laboratory |url=https://stfc.ukri.org/about-us/where-we-work/daresbury-laboratory/technology-at-daresbury/ }}</ref> and was Head of the Nuclear Physics Group<ref>{{citation |title=Nuclear Physics Group STFC Daresbury Laboratory |url=https://stfc.ukri.org/research/nuclear-physics/nuclear-physics-group/ }}</ref> at STFC [[Daresbury Laboratory]]. He is a visiting professor of physics at the [[University of Liverpool]]. 

==Biography==
Simpson was educated at [[University of Liverpool]] (BSc(Hons) Physics Class 1, 1979) and the [[University of Liverpool]] (PhD, 1983).

In 2016, he was awarded the Ernest Rutherford Medal and Prize by the [[Institute of Physics]]. The award recognises distinguished research in [[nuclear physics]] or [[nuclear technology]]. The award citation reads, "For his outstanding leadership in the development of new detector technologies and systems for experimental nuclear physics research within the UK and Europe, and for his seminal contributions to our understanding of the structure of atomic nuclei, especially in revealing new properties of nuclei at the limits of angular momentum, deformation, and stability".<ref>{{cite journal|url=http://www.nupecc.org/npn/npn271.pdf|title=The 2016 Ernest Rutherford Medal and Prize of the Institute of Physics |last1=M.A.Riley |journal=NuPECC Nuclear Physics News|volume=271 |page=37|year=2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Oliver Clay |title=Daresbury physicist receives top science prize previously awarded to Niels Bohr and Peter Higgs |date=6 July 2016|url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/news/daresbury-physicist-receives-top-science-11562285|newspaper=Liverpool Echo }}</ref>

An invited [[Open Access]] comment to a special [[Physica Scripta]] Focus issue celebrating the 40-year anniversary of the 1975 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] to [[Aage Bohr]], [[Ben Roy Mottelson]] and [[Leo Rainwater]] edited by Jerzy Dudek, outlines selected highlights from experimental investigations at the [[Niels Bohr Institute]], Denmark, and [[Daresbury Laboratory]], UK, in the late 1970s and early 1980s, many of which have continued at other national laboratories in Europe and the US to the present day.<ref>{{cite journal|title=High resolution gamma-ray spectroscopy and the fascinating angular momentum realm of the atomic nucleus |last1=M.A.Riley |last2=J.Simpson|last3=E.S.Paul|journal=Physica Scripta|volume=91 |article-number=123002|doi=10.1088/0031-8949/91/12/123002 |year=2016|issue=12 |bibcode=2016PhyS...91l3002R |doi-access=free }}</ref>
